title: Weekly pilot eval & threshold tweaks - Cerulean Analytics
meeting_header: Date: 2025-08-07 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Platform: Zoom | Recording: yes | Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Cerulean PM), Priya Nair (Cerulean Eng), Tom Benson (Cerulean DS), Ravi Kapoor (Cerulean Sec)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot evaluation metrics, triage regressions, and agree on prompt/threshold updates and security questions. Main topics: false-positive spike on classification route, scoring threshold adjustment experiment, guardrail suggestion, and next steps for a short benchmark run on dedicated nodes. Action items captured and demo of updated prompt set promised.
topics: regression analysis - spike in false positives
deployment options - hosted vs dedicated and VPC considerations
transcript: 00:00 Alex (AE): All right folks, thanks for joining. We're at our weekly Cerulean pilot sync - quick check: everyone seeing the agenda?
00:14 Jordan (Cerulean PM): Yep, looks good. We want to focus today on the sudden bump in false positives on the intent-classify route, and then the scoring thresholds Maya suggested.

00:29 Maya (SE): I pulled the heatmap and the batch of low-confidence samples, I think we can walk through the examples. Just a heads up I annotated about 40 cases in the sheet -- link in chat: tinyurl.com/cer-poc-heat
00:42 Priya (Eng): Got it, I opened the sheet. A couple of those look like prompt formatting artifacts, we saw some trailing tokens in the payloads from our client side.

00:57 Tom (DS): The false positive spike started after the latest dataset push on July 28th, so there's data drift probable. Our scoring currently uses threshold 0.6 for positive class, recall target was 0.78 but precision fell to 0.61.

01:15 Diego (Redwood SE): Thanks Tom. If I remember right the model variant you're on is redwood-open-1-ggml? or something — the trace says open-1-small and it was on hosted. Sometimes those labels get munged in the logs, we call it redwood-open-1-sm on our end.
01:34 Jordan: Yeah, model label mismatch shows up in the logs a lot, not a blocker but confusing. Priya, can you confirm environment — are you on Hosted API or Dedicated test pool for the last runs?

01:48 Priya: Hosted so far. We planned to spin up a dedicated node for the benchmark next week but haven't done it. Also we have VPC peering constraints so dedicated would need the VPC peering config.

02:03 Ravi (Security): On security, please loop in our infra folks if you plan a VPC, we need to validate SSO and KMS access. Also confirm audit log retention. We require SOC2 controls for production, right Alex?
02:18 Alex: Correct, SOC2 and we have KMS integrations. We'll send the SOC2 pack and KMS guide after the call. Diego, can you note that?
02:29 Diego: Yep noted. I'll share the Security & Compliance PDF and the KMS integration checklist to Jordan after this call.

02:42 Maya: Back to the spike: here's a representative example - prompt included enumerated bullets, and the model inferred user intent as 'cancel' when it should have been 'change date'. I suspect prompt template ambiguity and also KV cahce mismatch in the runtime causing context bleed.
03:01 Tom: We also have some duplicate examples in training that bias the model. I ran a quick confusion matrix and 'change date' got misclassified 18% as 'cancel' after that push.
03:16 Priya: So two levers: clean prompt templates (front-end) and adjust the scoring threshold; maybe lower recall target to improve precision?

03:29 Alex: Exactly - two concurrent experiments: A) prompt canonicalization + trimming of trailing newlines, B) threshold sweep from 0.6 to 0.72 to measure precision/recall. We can run both in parallel for a 24h window.
03:43 Jordan: Sounds good. Any risk with guardrails? We saw a couple of hallucination examples that the safety filter didn't catch.

03:52 Maya: The safety filter uses a keyword-list and model-confidence gating. For hallucinations, we recommend adding a stricter recall check for hallucination indicator and route to human fallback. But that increases latency.
04:07 Priya: Latency is important; our SLO is 300ms p95 for the user flows. Adding a human fallback will break that unless it's async. Can Redwood do async fallback and optimistic reply?
04:20 Diego: We support streaming and async callback patterns. For fallback we can respond with a 'we're verifying' placeholder then surface the human review later. That keeps UI latency low.
04:33 Tom: On evaluation metrics, can we add a weighted F-beta where false positives cost us 2x more than false negatives? That would align the threshold search with business impact.
04:45 Maya: Absolutely, we can run a threshold sweep optimizing for F2 (beta=2) or custom cost matrix. I'll attach the sweep script to the sheet.
04:58 Ravi: Quick sec - on encryption, does Redwood support customer-managed keys in the hosted mode or only on Private?
05:07 Alex: Hosted supports KMS integration with bring-your-own-key for enterprise tiers; Private gives you full HSM options. I'll include the KMS doc in the follow-up.
05:19 Jordan: Great. Back to regressions: are the flagged cases reproducible locally or are they environment-specific?
05:28 Priya: A mix. Some reproduce consistently when we re-send the exact payload, others only on 1 of 10 runs which suggests sampling nondeterminism or runtime caching differences.

05:41 Diego: Runtime nondeterminism can be from batching and seeding in the model. We can freeze the seed for benchmark runs. Also, prefix KV cache settings can cause older context tokens to bleed if not evicted properly.
05:56 Tom: Can you run the same subset on a dedicated node with fixed batch size and seed so we can compare?
06:04 Maya: Yes, I'll queue a dedicated 2-hour benchmark with fixed seed, batch=1 and deterministic mode on. Expect logs and raw outputs in the results folder.
06:15 Jordan: How long will the sweep take?
06:19 Maya: The threshold sweep across 0.5-0.8 with step 0.02 on ~2500 samples should finish in about 3h on dedicated, 6-8h on hosted depending on load.
06:31 Priya: We prefer dedicated for consistent numbers. We'll provision a small dedicated pool for the 3h run if you (Redwood) provide the template for VPC peering and firewall rules.
06:44 Diego: I'll send a checklist for dedicated provisioning and a sample terraform snippet for VPC peering after the call.
06:53 Tom: On prompt pruning, can we get Redwood's suggestion for which tokens to keep? Our prompts have a lot of meta text.
07:01 Maya: We'll provide a pruned canonical prompt set focusing on entity and intent only, trimmed of examples that increase jitter. We'll mark required vs optional tokens.
07:12 Jordan: Also a tiny bit about costs: what's the cost delta expected when we move from hosted to dedicated for our qps? We need a rough number for finance.
07:24 Alex: We'll send a cost estimate. Dedicated is a commit model; for a small pool, cost per token will drop ~25-40% depending on utilization. I'll include a cost model spreadsheet.
07:36 Priya: Any notes on model variants - would quantized models affect hallucination rate?
07:43 Maya: Quantized variants may slightly reduce hallucination but can affect semantic nuance. We can A/B test quantized vs full precision for a subset of inputs.
07:55 Jordan: Okay. Can we capture specific examples to seed guardrail rules? I added 12 in the sheet with the 'hallucination' tag.
08:05 Maya: Perfect. We'll incorporate those as deterministic checks in the guardrail engine and create a fallback policy for those triggers.
08:16 Tom: For the evaluation dashboard, can we get more granular histograms of confidence by intent? Right now we only see aggregate precision/recall.
08:26 Diego: We can add per-intent confidence distributions and a per-route token cost breakdown in the console for the pilot. I'll flag it as a request.
08:36 Jordan: On timeline - if we do the dedicated bench and prompt pruning this week, can we expect results by next Tuesday?
08:43 Maya: Yes, dedicated sweep today or tomorrow, pruning by EOD Tuesday, results early Wednesday. But timeline depends on dedicated provisioning speed.
08:55 Ravi: Security follow-ups: need role-based access and audit logs for the pilot. Do you have RBAC controls for team members?
09:03 Alex: Yes RBAC available on enterprise tier, with admin, dev, view roles. Audit logs we can stream to your SIEM via syslog or S3.
09:14 Priya: We'll want SSO mapped to Okta; that's our IdP.
09:19 Diego: We support SAML and OIDC; Okta is common. I'll include the SSO onboarding guide.
09:28 Jordan: Any competitors mentioned in the team? We're also evaluating Anthropic and Cohere for the semantics pipeline.
09:36 Alex: Noted. We'll include performance benchmarks comparing latency and per-token cost across the models you mentioned.
09:45 Tom: Quick question - when you do the threshold sweep, can you also calculate expected false-positive count per 10k requests? Helps with business impact modeling.
09:54 Maya: Yes, we'll include projected FP per 10k in the sweep output sheet.
10:02 Jordan: Great. Anything else on regression triage?
10:06 Priya: One more note: a subset of samples came from non-UTF char encodings, we may normalize upstream. I'll file a bug for our ingestion.
10:17 Alex: Cool. Let's recap actions and owners.
10:22 Diego: I'll share the Dedicated provisioning checklist, VPC peering terraform snippet, and the SSO/KMS docs (due 2025-08-08).
10:36 Maya: I'll run the threshold sweep on dedicated, produce the per-intent confidence histograms, attach the sweep script and results (due 2025-08-11).
10:48 Tom: We'll sample and label an extra 500 edge cases for the next run and tag them in the sheet (Tom, due 2025-08-10).
10:58 Priya: We'll provision the small dedicated pool and open a ticket with infra for VPC peering (Priya, due 2025-08-09).
11:08 Jordan: I'll review the guardrail examples and add 8 more if needed (Jordan, due 2025-08-09).
11:18 Ravi: I'll verify compliance requirements and share SOC2 questions (Ravi, due 2025-08-10).
11:30 Alex: I'll send SOC2 pack, cost model spreadsheet, and the KMS integration guide (Alex, due 2025-08-08).
11:42 Diego: Sharing the resources in the chat now - short links to docs and the spreadsheet.
11:55 Speaker 2: (crosstalk) also - the sample id 4432 looks like it had a truncated p...
12:05 Maya: noted, we flagged truncation as a possible cause. We'll add a check to reject payloads under 80 chars if they appear truncated.
12:18 Jordan: Ok thanks everyone. Let's reconvene same time next week - unless we need a mid-week demo after the dedicated run.
12:30 Alex: Works for Redwood. We'll aim to have the sweep results and the pruned prompt deck before Wednesday and set a mid-week review if something critical appears.
12:45 Priya: Thanks all. Meeting end.
